newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria denies maltreatment of street children.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria denies maltreatment of street children.

text.p: Bulgaria's education ministry on Friday dismissed a report by a U.S.-based human rights group that accused authorities of using violence and intimidation against street children.

"Bulgaria has never abused its street children and the reports's findings are a mere insinuation aimed only to harm the country's image," the head of the special schools department at the ministry, Georgi Dodov, told Reuters.
The Human Rights Watch group on Thursday accused Bulgarian authorities of using violence and arbitrary arrest against the country's street children, who are mostly of Gypsy origin.
It also condemned the practice of sending troublesome minors to workhouse-style institutions where conditions are usually very hard.
"The report's findings are absolutely unfounded. They are based on anonymous reports and give no definite names," Dodov said.

However he said there had been three recent cases of violence being used against children in the special schools and one institution was shut down last year following reports of systematic torture by its teachers.
"But these were isolated cases and the perpetrators were immediately sacked," Dodov added.
He said his ministry was working in close cooperation with the police to ease the problems facing street children.
"Bulgaria's education ministry, interior ministry and the chief prosecution are expected in the coming days to officially respond to the report's outrageous accusations," Dodov said.
An estimated 14,000 children scrape a living on Bulgaria's streets by begging, pickpocketing and sifting through rubbish heaps.

Many Bulgarians have little sympathy for the plight of the street children, whom they regard as a major source of petty crime. They say the children's parents encourage them to beg and steal instead of sending them to school.
